study: Finkelstein et al. 2010, Problem Based Economics (Buck Institute), NCEE 2010-4002 / REL West
eval_evidence: REL West / WestEd contractor evaluation (NCEE 2010-4002); 'Neither the authors nor WestEd and its key staff have financial' stake; Buck Institute (developer) is acknowledged separately.
developer_evidence: 'The Buck Institute provided trainers who were current or former economics' teachers; the developer (Buck Institute) supplied/led the 5-day, 40-hr PD workshop.
cascade_evidence: Buck Institute provided expert-teacher trainers who introduced the curriculum to teachers in a 5-day workshop directly; no train-the-trainer / school-cascade hop.
counterfactual_evidence: 'Teachers in control schools participated in their regular annual professional development' and taught BAU high-school economics; no active alternative program.
coaching_evidence: Beyond the summer workshop, support was 'a series of five scheduled phone conferences with fellow participating teachers' to discuss pacing/challenges; no in-class coaching.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention = Problem Based Economics curriculum + teacher PD for the regular one-semester economics course; no tutoring/pull-out/extra minutes or student software dose.
maturity_evidence: Curriculum/PD delivered once for a single one-semester economics course (PD summer 2007, course spring 2008, outcomes at semester end); no multi-year maturity axis (and first time teachers used it).
